output.sql:
WITH customer_revenue AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2024 THEN net_revenue END) AS rev_2024,
    SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2025 THEN net_revenue END) AS rev_2025
  FROM marts.fct_orders
  WHERE is_revenue = true
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count
FROM customer_revenue
WHERE rev_2024 > 0
  AND COALESCE(rev_2025, 0) < 0.5 * rev_2024
output.explanation: Revenue is defined as orders with is_revenue = true, measured by net_revenue and grouped by the calendar year of order_date. The query sums each customer's 2024 and 2025 revenue, then counts customers with positive 2024 revenue whose 2025 revenue (treating no 2025 orders as zero) is below half of their 2024 revenue.
